chunks: And regarding what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hariz, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Breastfeeding does not cause prohibition (of marriage) except if it is performed by a woman who is compelled, or a servant, or a wet-nurse, and then she breastfeeds ten times, causing the boy to be satiated and to sleep. This report also does not contradict what we have previously presented, because its apparent meaning is set aside by consensus, since a woman who is neither compelled, nor a servant, nor a wet-nurse can still cause prohibition through breastfeeding, whether she is a woman volunteering to breastfeed a child, or she was asked to do so, or due to other causes leading to that. It is also possible that the intended meaning here is the negation of prohibition for one who breastfeeds him once or twice.

key_terms.مَتْرُوكُ الظَّاهِر: The apparent meaning is set aside (abrogated/qualified)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for breastfeeding to make two people mahram (unmarriageable)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between this report and others by interpreting the mention of 'compelled' or 'servant' women as a specific example rather than an exhaustive list, thereby affirming that voluntary breastfeeding also establishes prohibition. He further clarifies that the ten feedings must be sufficient to satisfy the child's hunger, distinguishing this from mere trial feedings, while explicitly ruling out one or two feedings as insufficient for creating mahramiyyah. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of reconciling seemingly conflicting narrations through contextual interpretation (ta'wil) rather than abrogation.
